Unlike Treasury or tariff money, private funds don’t require congressional approval. 

The Appropriations Clause only applies to money drawn from the U.S. Treasury,  private donations sit outside that rule.

Key differences:
• Donors (not Congress) set eligibility, conditions, and timing 
• No deficit or “taxpayer money” criticism 
 
A real example: 
Michael Dell and his wife Susan pledged $6.25 billion in private funds to seed “Trump Accounts,” depositing $250 into investment accounts for roughly 25 million children. That portion didn’t need a new congressional appropriation because it was their money, not Treasury funds.

Private capital removes any legal barriers  💥
